newsitem.title: USA: Weekend rain forecast for southern U.S. Midwest.
newsitem.headline: Weekend rain forecast for southern U.S. Midwest.

text.p: Rain was forecast to spread across the southern Midwest Saturday and Sunday, bringing up to an inch in areas across southern portions of Missouri, Illinois, Indiana, and Ohio, meteorlogists said.
Except for northern Iowa and southern Minnesota, the rest of the Midwest should remain dry until Monday when a new storm system enters the area.
Scattered light showers may dip into southern Minnesota and northern Iowa Sunday from the north.
Showers were forecast Monday and Tuesday in the western Midwest and in the eastern Midwest Tuesday and Wednesday.
"It isn't very optimistic for the soft red winter wheat harvest," said Joel Burgio, Weather Services Corp meteorologist, of the wet weather.
However, the moisture should be beneficial for corn and soybeans.
Rain amounts early next week should range from 0.5 to 1.5 inches with 60 to 70 percent coverage, said Fred Gesser, Weather Express Inc meteorologist.
During the rain high temperatures should dip down to the upper 70s and low 80s Fahrenheit, but return to the 80s and possibly mid-90s once the storms pass.

Gesser said a high pressure system should spread into the Midwest July 6 to 10, with high temperatures averaging in the 90s. Some nighttime rain may occur, but otherwise the period should be dry for the Midwest.
